target.title: fix(macos): fit onboarding window on short screens
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #98674.

The macOS onboarding window used a fixed preferred content height and `window.center()`, so on short visible desktop areas the first-run window could extend below the screen and hide the bottom setup/navigation action.

## Why This Change Was Made

This routes onboarding window placement through the existing `WindowPlacement.centeredFrame` helper so the actual NSWindow frame is clamped to the active screen visible frame before display. The SwiftUI root view now allows its height to shrink between the onboarding minimum and preferred height, so the clamped window can adapt instead of insisting on the full preferred height.

## User Impact

Users on shorter displays or desktops with reduced visible height should be able to see and click the onboarding bottom actions instead of getting stuck during first-run setup.

## Evidence

- Added `WindowPlacementTests` coverage for onboarding frame clamping on a 690pt short visible frame and for preserving preferred height on tall screens.
- `git diff --check`
- Attempted: `swift test --package-path apps/macos --filter WindowPlacementTests` and `swift test --package-path apps/macos --filter OnboardingViewSmokeTests`; both are blocked locally because `apps/macos` requires Swift tools 6.2.0 while this machine has Apple Swift 6.1.

target.title: fix(slack): log native progress stream start failures instead of silently swallowing
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When native Slack progress streaming starts, overlapping progress callbacks can await the same in-flight `startSlackStream` promise. The **initiating** `updateNativeProgressStream()` path already reports failures via `runtime.error`, but the prior PR added a second `logVerbose` in the waiter catch — duplicating diagnostics for one rejection.

## Changes

- **Remove duplicate waiter logging** — `waitForNativeProgressStreamStart()` keeps a silent catch that only marks `streamFailed` and returns `false`.
- **Improve single-owner diagnostic** — initiating `updateNativeProgressStream()` now reports `start` vs `update` phase in the existing `runtime.error` message.
- **Add production-equivalent overlap regression** — uses the real `createChannelProgressDraftGate` with staggered overlapping progress callbacks; asserts exactly **one** `runtime.error` and **no** waiter `logVerbose` duplicate.

## Evidence

**Current head:** `94aad230`

**Regression tests:**
```

→ 2 passed
```

target.title: fix: suspension and restart wait for background execs
target.body:
Fixes #104079

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where hosts using cooperative Gateway suspension or safe restart could receive an idle result while an approved background exec process was still running. A visible process entry could also be removed before the operating-system process had actually exited, leaving the remaining work unaccounted for.

## Why This Change Was Made

The process registry now retains a count-only live background-exec marker through confirmed exit. Detached approval execution atomically hands work from Gateway root admission to that marker, while suspension and every safe-restart path account for both sides of the handoff. The protocol exposes only an aggregate `background-exec` blocker; commands, PIDs, output, and session identifiers remain private.

## User Impact

Hosting controllers no longer freeze, snapshot, or restart the Gateway across a live background command. `process remove` can still hide a session immediately, but lifecycle admission remains blocked until the process owner confirms exit.

Release-note context: cooperative suspension and safe restart now wait for live background exec sessions.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `blue-prawn` / [run 29139283576](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29139283576): 207 focused test executions passed across registry, detached approval, suspension, restart, reload, and protocol suites.

target.title: fix(web-fetch): recover from stale runtime providers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Runtime web-fetch metadata can retain a selected provider id that is no longer available in the current provider list. When the user did not explicitly configure that provider, resolution returned no provider instead of falling back to the current auto-detected provider.

## Why This Change Was Made

The resolver now treats an explicit `providerId` as authoritative and fail-closed, while allowing stale runtime `selectedProvider` metadata to fall back to auto-detection. This keeps explicit config strict without letting old runtime state disable web fetch.

When stale runtime metadata is normalized for the fallback provider, the provider-facing `selectedProviderKeySource` is also cleared. That source describes the selected provider's credential, so preserving `"missing"` or another source from the removed provider would mislead plugin runtime behavior.

## User Impact

Users recover web fetch automatically after provider metadata becomes stale, while invalid explicit provider configuration still fails clearly. Providers no longer receive a fallback `selectedProvider` paired with a credential-source value from the removed provider.

## Evidence

- `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=redacted-firecrawl-key node --import tsx - <<'NODE' ... NODE` against head `fe452da3b7502ec2e492b0c7924dc638851db06e`: real web-fetch runtime/provider discovery selected `firecrawl` from stale `removed-provider` runtime metadata, with the env key redacted.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/web-content-core/src/provider-runtime-shared.test.ts src/web-fetch/runtime.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` - 2 files / 32 tests passed.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check packages/web-content-core/src/provider-runtime-shared.ts packages/web-content-core/src/provider-runtime-shared.test.ts src/web-fetch/runtime.test.ts`
- `OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs packages/web-content-core/src/provider-runtime-shared.ts packages/web-content-core/src/provider-runtime-shared.test.ts src/web-fetch/runtime.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --engine claude` - clean, no accepted/actionable findings. Default Codex autoreview could not reach the model because the local OpenAI API key returned 401 before review.

## Proof

The runtime proof used real `resolveWebFetchDefinition` and bundled Firecrawl provider discovery, not mocked provider lists. Output:

```json
{
  "env": {
    "FIRECRAWL_API_KEY": "<redacted>"
  },
  "staleRuntimeSelectedProvider": "removed-provider",
  "resolvedProvider": "firecrawl",
  "toolDescription": "Fetch a page using Firecrawl.",
  "originalRuntimeMetadataUnchanged": {
    "providerConfigured": "removed-provider",
    "providerSource": "configured",
    "selectedProvider": "removed-provider",
    "selectedProviderKeySource": "missing",
    "diagnostics": []
  }
}
```

The focused regression tests cover both layers: the shared resolver clears stale `selectedProviderKeySource` in the normalized provider-facing metadata copy, and the web-fetch runtime still leaves the original runtime metadata object unchanged.

target.title: feat(write): add append mode to prevent silent data loss
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The write tool always overwrites files. An `append: true` parameter lets the agent add content to the end of an existing file instead of replacing it. The agent requested this capability repeatedly in real sessions — it wants to write logs, build up checklists incrementally, and extend existing scripts without re-reading them first.

## Why This Change Was Made

Write-tool silent data loss (#40001) can happen when an agent writes to a file it has already edited without re-reading the current content. An append mode gives the agent a safer option: it can add new content without risking the loss of previous edits.

## What Changed

- `src/agents/sessions/tools/write.ts` — add `append?: boolean` to the schema, `WriteOperations.appendFile` method, append branch in `execute`, and append-aware recovery (`isRecoveredAppendContent`).
- `src/agents/sessions/tools/tool-contracts.ts` — add `append?: boolean` to `WriteToolInput`.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.read.ts` — wire `appendFile` for host (`fs.appendFile`), workspace (`root.append()`), and sandbox (read-modify-write, since the sandbox bridge has no native append).
- `src/agents/sessions/tools/write.test.ts` — 5 new tests: basic append, append-to-new-file, no-op short-circuit for overwrite, malformed append param rejection, and append-identical-content preserving duplicates.

## User Impact

- `append: true` is opt-in. The default write behavior is unchanged.
- Append to a non-existent file creates it (matching `>>` shell semantics).
- The write tool description and prompt snippet advertise the new parameter.

## Evidence

Focused suite (local fallback — Crabbox unavailable in this env):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/sessions/tools/write.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

target.title: fix(agent-tools): add request timeout to remote media fetches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The agent-side image, image-generation, and PDF tools fetch remote media through `loadWebMedia` / `loadWebMediaRaw` with only a body-idle gap guard (`readIdleTimeoutMs`). A remote endpoint that accepts the TCP connection but withholds response headers forever leaves the fetch open indefinitely — `readIdleTimeoutMs` only governs gaps between body chunks, never the pre-header stall. This PR threads a 15-minute header-arrival deadline through the three agent-tool call sites so a never-responding endpoint fails fast while slow-but-progressing transfers keep going.

## Why This Change Was Made

The initial proposal exposed a new `WebMediaOptions.timeoutMs?: number` (overall-request lifetime). ClawSweeper correctly rejected that as compatibility-breaking: it would have capped healthy bodies that keep yielding past 15 minutes. The narrower `FetchMediaOptions.responseHeaderTimeoutMs` seam landed on `origin/main` via PR #103020 (merge commit `26aef8c48bc40d2ea456c2cfc3eca126dca33888`, 2026-07-10 13:31 UTC, currently reachable from `origin/main@bb26753705`) specifically for this stall class — header-only deadline via `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`, `cleanup()`-ed once headers arrive so the body is not capped. This PR drops the parallel total-timeout surface and adopts that canonical seam end-to-end through the three agent-tool call sites.

## What Changed

- `src/media/web-media.ts` — `WebMediaOptions.timeoutMs?: number` removed; replaced with `WebMediaOptions.responseHeaderTimeoutMs?: number`. `loadWebMediaInternal` destructures the new field and forwards it conditionally into `readRemoteMediaBuffer({ ..., responseHeaderTimeoutMs })` so an unset value does not overwrite main's "no header deadline" default.
- `src/agents/tools/media-tool-shared.ts` — new export `REMOTE_MEDIA_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS = 15 * 60_000` next to the existing `REMOTE_MEDIA_READ_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000`.
- `src/agents/tools/image-tool.ts:1042`, `image-generate-tool.ts:675`, `pdf-tool.ts:487` — on the `isHttpUrl` branch, the spread becomes `{ readIdleTimeoutMs: REMOTE_MEDIA_READ_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS, responseHeaderTimeoutMs: REMOTE_MEDIA_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS }`.
- `src/agents/tools/{image,image-generate,pdf}-tool.test.ts` — the prior `timeoutMs: 15 * 60_000` assertions added by the previous version of this branch are removed (the canonical seam is now exercised end-to-end via the `loadWebMedia` forwarding layer; per-tool assertions would be redundant).
- `proof-103209-image-tool-layer.mts` — new live-run proof that exercises the canonical seam end-to-end through `loadWebMedia` (the entrypoint image-tool/image-generate-tool/pdf-tool invoke), real stalled HTTP server, real AbortSignal, surfaced error shape.

## User Impact

- Hard 15-minute upper bound on header-arrival latency for image, image-generation, and PDF tool calls against stalled remote endpoints.
- Healthy upstreams see no behavior change. **Slow-but-progressing transfers are explicitly NOT capped** — once headers arrive, the header deadline is cleared and `readIdleTimeoutMs` (120s for agent-tools) continues to bound chunk gaps.
- Users on very slow networks where headers legitimately take >15 min will see new failures. This matches the existing 15-minute ceiling from canonical precedent #103266 (`src/cli/nodes-camera.ts:20`, `CAMERA_URL_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS`); the trade-off has already been accepted by maintainers on that merge.

## Evidence

### Live behavior proof (image-tool entrypoint `loadWebMedia`, real HTTP server, real fetch, real AbortSignal, surfaced error shape)

Local fallback run (Crabbox unavailable in this env):

```
$ node node_modules/.bin/tsx proof-103209-image-tool-layer.mts
[proof] stalled HTTP server listening on http://127.0.0.1:35937
[proof] calling loadWebMedia (the entrypoint image-tool/image-generate-tool/pdf-tool invoke)
[proof] with responseHeaderTimeoutMs=1000ms (production uses 15*60_000)
[proof] this exercises the canonical seam from PR #103020:
[proof]   loadWebMedia -> readRemoteMediaBuffer -> fetchGuardedMediaResponse
[proof]   -> fetchWithSsrFGuard -> buildTimeoutAbortSignal (response header deadline)
[proof]   -> globalThis.fetch
[proof] elapsed: 1160ms
[proof] surfaced error.name: MediaFetchError
[proof] surfaced error.code: fetch_failed
[proof] surfaced error.message: Failed to fetch media from http://127.0.0.1:35937/never-responds.png: request timed out
[proof] surfaced error.cause.name: TimeoutError
[proof] surfaced error.cause.message: request timed out
[proof] result: responseHeaderTimeoutMs fired through real production path
{
  "url": "http://127.0.0.1:35937/never-responds.png",
  "responseHeaderTimeoutMs": 1000,
  "outcome": {
    "kind": "error",
    "name": "MediaFetchError",
    "code": "fetch_failed",
    "message": "Failed to fetch media from http://127.0.0.1:35937/never-responds.png: request timed out",
    "causeName": "TimeoutError",
    "causeMessage": "request timed out",
    "elapsedMs": 1160
  },
  "passed": true
}
```

Key observations:
- **1160ms elapsed** (vs 1000ms `responseHeaderTimeoutMs`): the canonical seam fires at the deadline.
- **Surfaced error shape**: `MediaFetchError { code: "fetch_failed", cause: TimeoutError("request timed out") }` — the exact error the image tool's `execute` function throws when the underlying fetch stalls. The agent runtime will surface a clean "request timed out" error to the caller instead of hanging.

### Repository test (forwards responseHeaderTimeoutMs through the public seam)

The forwarding test ("forwards responseHeaderTimeoutMs from loadWebMediaRaw through readRemoteMediaBuffer") lives on the companion branch #103206 in `src/media/web-media.test.ts`. Both branches share the same `WebMediaOptions` / `loadWebMediaInternal` forwarding code (this branch carries it for standalone typecheck; #103206 is the canonical owner of the seam), so the test exercises the same code path that image-tool / image-generate-tool / pdf-tool call into.

Focused suite runs (local fallback — Crabbox unavailable in this env):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/tools/image-tool.test.ts src/agents/tools/image-generate-tool.test.ts src/agents/tools/pdf-tool.test.ts --reporter=verbose
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  180 passed (180)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/media/web-media.test.ts src/media/fetch.test.ts --reporter=verbose
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  121 passed (121)
```

### Canonical precedents

- **PR #103020 / merge `26aef8c48bc40d2ea456c2cfc3eca126dca33888`** — `FetchMediaOptions.responseHeaderTimeoutMs` at `src/media/fetch.ts:82`; the canonical seam.
- **PR #103266 / merge `541c9f0bf01712d81d5217eb2a5c15d05686259d`** — canonical 15-minute bounded-media ceiling from `src/cli/nodes-camera.ts:20`. This PR reuses the same ceiling on the narrower header-only deadline.
- **Telegram precedent** — `extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.resolve-media-retry.ts:356` already uses `TELEGRAM_DOWNLOAD_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000`. This PR's constant name mirrors that pattern.

## Coordination with #103206

With the canonical seam now on `origin/main`, both this PR and #103206 independently use that seam — they no longer duplicate each other and either can land in any order. No cross-repo stacking required. The forwarding test on #103206 covers the same `WebMediaOptions` → `loadWebMediaInternal` → `readRemoteMediaBuffer` path that this branch's three agent-tool call sites invoke. After #103206 lands, this branch can drop its duplicate `src/media/web-media.ts` forwarding changes (the seam becomes part of `main`).


## Post-review updates (2026-07-11)

ClawSweeper re-review (2026-07-11 03:39 UTC) identified one P1 finding:

### Covered video_generate

`video_generate` also loads reference assets through `loadWebMedia` but was omitted from the deadline rollout. Added `responseHeaderTimeoutMs: REMOTE_MEDIA_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS` to both the sandbox and non-sandbox `loadWebMedia` calls in `src/agents/tools/video-generate-tool.ts:633-642`.

### Focused regression test for video_generate

Added `applies the shared response-header deadline when loading remote reference assets` in `src/agents/tools/video-generate-tool.test.ts`. It mocks `loadWebMedia` and asserts the call receives the canonical 15-minute header deadline. Verified by temporarily removing the deadline from `video-generate-tool.ts` — the test then fails because `responseHeaderTimeoutMs` is `undefined`.

### Removed PR-specific proof script

Deleted `proof-103209-image-tool-layer.mts`.

### Verification

```
      Tests  39 passed (39)

$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/tools/video-generate-tool.ts src/agents/tools/video-generate-tool.test.ts
```

## Post-review updates (2026-07-11 round 2)

ClawSweeper re-review (2026-07-11 05:29 UTC) identified one P2 finding:

### Removed ineffective video timeout path

Remote HTTP(S) URLs in `video_generate` are returned early as provider URLs at the top of `loadReferenceAssets` (lines 596-601), bypassing `loadWebMedia` entirely. The `responseHeaderTimeoutMs` on the `loadWebMedia` calls only affected local/data input paths. Removed from both sandbox and non-sandbox branches in `src/agents/tools/video-generate-tool.ts`, along with the associated regression test and `REMOTE_MEDIA_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS` import.

The image, image-generation, and PDF tool paths (which DO route remote URLs through `loadWebMedia`) remain unchanged with their 15-min header deadline.

target.title: fix(agents): honor Anthropic Retry-After in auto-retry backoff (#103849)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On the default Anthropic Messages transport (used by every `anthropic-messages` model), a 429 response carrying a server-specified `Retry-After` header is turned into a plain `Error` with no status or retry-after data attached. `AgentSession.prepareRetry` therefore always falls back to fixed exponential backoff (2s / 4s / 8s) regardless of the server's cooldown. With `maxRetries: 3`, all three retries can land inside a still-active 30-second rate-limit window and the turn fails outright instead of succeeding after the server's actual cooldown.

Closes #103849

## Why This Change Was Made

The bespoke fetch client behind the managed transport is not a Stainless-style SDK, so the `Retry-After` value parsed upstream is only used to set an `x-should-retry` header this client never reads. The header is discarded before the error reaches `prepareRetry`, whose delay formula has no input for a server-prescribed wait.

## Changes

- **`src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.ts`** — non-OK responses throw via `createAnthropicMessagesHttpError`, attaching `status`/`httpStatus` and a `retryAfterSeconds` parsed with the **canonical** `parseRetryAfterSeconds` (now exported from `provider-transport-fetch.ts` — no divergent duplicate).
- **`src/agents/transport-stream-shared.ts`** — `extractTransportErrorDetails` propagates `httpStatus`/`retryAfterSeconds` from the thrown error onto the AssistantMessage.
- **`packages/llm-core/src/types.ts`** — `AssistantMessage` gains optional `httpStatus?` / `retryAfterSeconds?` (additive; no migration required).
- **`src/llm/utils/retry.ts`** — `resolveAutoRetryDelayMs` uses the server cooldown as a lower bound for the exponential delay, bounded by the operator-configured `retry.provider.maxRetryDelayMs` (default 60s). It lives here (not in the session module) so it is not re-exported through the plugin-sdk barrel, keeping the public SDK surface unchanged.
- **`src/agents/sessions/agent-session.ts`** — `prepareRetry` passes `getProviderRetrySettings().maxRetryDelayMs` and handles the reject case.

### Retry-After bound (respects existing config; no arbitrary ceiling)

The ceiling is the existing operator setting `retry.provider.maxRetryDelayMs` (default 60s, "max server-requested delay before failing"), not a magic number:

- A cooldown **within** the configured max is honored **in full** — including values above 60s when the operator raises the limit (never silently shortened into the active window).
- A cooldown that **exceeds** the configured max returns `null`, so `prepareRetry` **stops retrying in-turn** and lets provider fallback / operator recovery proceed — instead of holding the session asleep for minutes or hours. This resolves the `merge-risk: availability` and `merge-risk: compatibility` concerns.
- An overflowed/malformed numeric header (canonical parser yields `Infinity`) is rejected, not silently collapsed to the short exponential schedule.

## User Impact

Anthropic 429s with a `Retry-After` within the configured tolerance now delay the automatic retry by at least the server window (so rate-limited turns wait out the cooldown and succeed); cooldowns beyond the tolerance fail fast for fallback rather than stalling the session.

## Evidence

**Real behavior proof (end to end, accepted + rejected).** A real Node HTTP server on `127.0.0.1` responds with HTTP 429 + a `Retry-After` header, driven through the real `createAnthropicMessagesTransportStreamFn()` (real `buildGuardedModelFetch`); the stub endpoint is the only mock. The propagated `retryAfterSeconds` is fed into the real `resolveAutoRetryDelayMs` with the default `maxRetryDelayMs=60000`:

```
configured maxRetryDelayMs=60000
ACCEPTED (retry-after: 30):  httpStatus=429 retryAfterSeconds=30  -> prepareRetry delay=30000ms
REJECTED (retry-after: 120): httpStatus=429 retryAfterSeconds=120 -> prepareRetry delay=null (stop retrying -> fallback)
```

Before this fix (origin/main) the same 429 yields `httpStatus=null`, `retryAfterSeconds=null`, and a fixed 2000ms backoff.

**Focused tests.**
- `src/llm/utils/retry.auto-retry-delay.test.ts` — exponential fallback, lower-bound, boundary at max, reject above max, reject `Infinity`, honor >60s when the operator raises the max, invalid-hint fallback.
- `src/agents/provider-transport-fetch.test.ts` — canonical `parseRetryAfterSeconds` across all forms + overflow header → `Infinity`.
- `src/agents/transport-stream-shared.test.ts` — status/retry-after propagation onto the AssistantMessage.

```
$ npx vitest run src/llm/utils/retry.auto-retry-delay.test.ts src/llm/utils/retry.test.ts \
```

target.title: fix(agent-tools): add request timeout to remote media fetches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The agent-side image, image-generation, and PDF tools fetch remote media through `loadWebMedia` / `loadWebMediaRaw` with only a body-idle gap guard (`readIdleTimeoutMs`). A remote endpoint that accepts the TCP connection but withholds response headers forever leaves the fetch open indefinitely — `readIdleTimeoutMs` only governs gaps between body chunks, never the pre-header stall. This PR threads a 15-minute header-arrival deadline through the three agent-tool call sites so a never-responding endpoint fails fast while slow-but-progressing transfers keep going.

## Why This Change Was Made

The initial proposal exposed a new `WebMediaOptions.timeoutMs?: number` (overall-request lifetime). ClawSweeper correctly rejected that as compatibility-breaking: it would have capped healthy bodies that keep yielding past 15 minutes. The narrower `FetchMediaOptions.responseHeaderTimeoutMs` seam landed on `origin/main` via PR #103020 (merge commit `26aef8c48bc40d2ea456c2cfc3eca126dca33888`, 2026-07-10 13:31 UTC, currently reachable from `origin/main@bb26753705`) specifically for this stall class — header-only deadline via `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`, `cleanup()`-ed once headers arrive so the body is not capped. This PR drops the parallel total-timeout surface and adopts that canonical seam end-to-end through the three agent-tool call sites.

## What Changed

- `src/media/web-media.ts` — `WebMediaOptions.timeoutMs?: number` removed; replaced with `WebMediaOptions.responseHeaderTimeoutMs?: number`. `loadWebMediaInternal` destructures the new field and forwards it conditionally into `readRemoteMediaBuffer({ ..., responseHeaderTimeoutMs })` so an unset value does not overwrite main's "no header deadline" default.
- `src/agents/tools/media-tool-shared.ts` — new export `REMOTE_MEDIA_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS = 15 * 60_000` next to the existing `REMOTE_MEDIA_READ_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000`.
- `src/agents/tools/image-tool.ts:1042`, `image-generate-tool.ts:675`, `pdf-tool.ts:487` — on the `isHttpUrl` branch, the spread becomes `{ readIdleTimeoutMs: REMOTE_MEDIA_READ_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS, responseHeaderTimeoutMs: REMOTE_MEDIA_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS }`.
- `src/agents/tools/{image,image-generate,pdf}-tool.test.ts` — the prior `timeoutMs: 15 * 60_000` assertions added by the previous version of this branch are removed (the canonical seam is now exercised end-to-end via the `loadWebMedia` forwarding layer; per-tool assertions would be redundant).
- `proof-103209-image-tool-layer.mts` — new live-run proof that exercises the canonical seam end-to-end through `loadWebMedia` (the entrypoint image-tool/image-generate-tool/pdf-tool invoke), real stalled HTTP server, real AbortSignal, surfaced error shape.

## User Impact

- Hard 15-minute upper bound on header-arrival latency for image, image-generation, and PDF tool calls against stalled remote endpoints.
- Healthy upstreams see no behavior change. **Slow-but-progressing transfers are explicitly NOT capped** — once headers arrive, the header deadline is cleared and `readIdleTimeoutMs` (120s for agent-tools) continues to bound chunk gaps.
- Users on very slow networks where headers legitimately take >15 min will see new failures. target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadWebMedia` / `readRemoteMediaBuffer` had no upper bound on header-arrival latency. An unresponsive upstream could pin a Tlon media download or URL-backed image upload at the TCP/streaming-read layer until `readIdleTimeoutMs` finally tripped — and only if a body ever started. This PR threads a 15-minute header-arrival deadline through `WebMediaOptions` and the two Tlon call sites so a never-responding endpoint fails fast while slow-but-progressing transfers keep going.

## Why This Change Was Made

The initial proposal exposed a new `WebMediaOptions.timeoutMs?: number` (overall-request lifetime). ClawSweeper correctly rejected that as compatibility-breaking: it would have capped healthy bodies that keep yielding past 15 minutes. The narrower `FetchMediaOptions.responseHeaderTimeoutMs` seam landed on `origin/main` via PR #103020 (merge commit `26aef8c48bc40d2ea456c2cfc3eca126dca33888`, 2026-07-10 13:31 UTC, currently reachable from `origin/main@bb26753705`) specifically for this stall class — header-only deadline via `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`, `cleanup()`-ed once headers arrive so the body is not capped. This PR drops the parallel total-timeout surface and adopts that canonical seam end-to-end.

## What Changed

- `src/media/web-media.ts` — `WebMediaOptions.timeoutMs?: number` removed; replaced with `WebMediaOptions.responseHeaderTimeoutMs?: number`. `loadWebMediaInternal` destructures the new field and forwards it conditionally into `readRemoteMediaBuffer({ ..., responseHeaderTimeoutMs })` so an unset value does not overwrite main's "no header deadline" default.
- `src/media/web-media.test.ts` — replaces the prior "aborts a … via the overall timeoutMs deadline" test with **"forwards responseHeaderTimeoutMs from loadWebMediaRaw through readRemoteMediaBuffer"** (using `vi.useFakeTimers()` + a progressing body stream, identical to main's `fetch.test.ts:438-485` "clears the response-header deadline while a healthy body keeps progressing" pattern). Asserts the resolved buffer contains the enqueued bytes after the header deadline clears — proving the public seam actually forwards the field.
- `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/media.ts` — replaces `TLON_MEDIA_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS` with `TLON_MEDIA_DOWNLOAD_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS = 15 * 60_000`; `downloadMedia`'s `fetchOptions` now forwards `responseHeaderTimeoutMs:` to both `saveRemoteMedia` and `readRemoteMediaBuffer`.
- `extensions/tlon/src/urbit/upload.ts` — replaces `TLON_UPLOAD_IMAGE_TIMEOUT_MS` with `TLON_UPLOAD_IMAGE_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS = 15 * 60_000`; `uploadImageFromUrl`'s `readRemoteMediaBuffer` call forwards the same.
- `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/media.test.ts`, `extensions/tlon/src/urbit/upload.test.ts` — assertion relaxed to `expect.objectContaining({ ..., responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 15 * 60_000 })`.
- `proof-103206-tool-run.mts` — new live-run proof that exercises the canonical seam end-to-end (real stalled HTTP server + real `loadWebMedia` + real AbortSignal + surfaced error shape).

## User Impact

- Hard 15-minute upper bound on header-arrival latency for Tlon media downloads and URL-backed image uploads triggered by `extensions/tlon`.
- Healthy upstreams see no behavior change. **Slow-but-progressing transfers are explicitly NOT capped** — once headers arrive, the header deadline is cleared and `readIdleTimeoutMs` (30s for Tlon) continues to bound chunk gaps. This is the deliberate behavior change vs. the prior total-timeout proposal.
- Tlon users on very slow networks where headers legitimately take >15 min will see new failures. This matches the existing 15-minute ceiling from canonical precedent #103266 (`src/cli/nodes-camera.ts:20`, `CAMERA_URL_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS`); the trade-off has already been accepted by maintainers on that merge.

Key observations:

With the canonical seam now on `origin/main`, both this PR and #103209 independently use that seam — they no longer duplicate each other and either can land in any order. The original forwarding test created the `Response` synchronously, so headers were already available even if `responseHeaderTimeoutMs` was dropped. target.title: feat(write): add append mode to prevent silent data loss
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The write tool always overwrites files. An `append: true` parameter lets the agent add content to the end of an existing file instead of replacing it. The agent requested this capability repeatedly in real sessions — it wants to write logs, build up checklists incrementally, and extend existing scripts without re-reading them first.

## Why This Change Was Made

Write-tool silent data loss (#40001) can happen when an agent writes to a file it has already edited without re-reading the current content. An append mode gives the agent a safer option: it can add new content without risking the loss of previous edits.

## What Changed

- `src/agents/sessions/tools/write.ts` — add `append?: boolean` to the schema, `WriteOperations.appendFile` method, append branch in `execute`, and append-aware recovery (`isRecoveredAppendContent`).
- `src/agents/sessions/tools/tool-contracts.ts` — add `append?: boolean` to `WriteToolInput`.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.read.ts` — wire `appendFile` for host (`fs.appendFile`), workspace (`root.append()`), and sandbox (read-modify-write, since the sandbox bridge has no native append).
- `src/agents/sessions/tools/write.test.ts` — 5 new tests: basic append, append-to-new-file, no-op short-circuit for overwrite, malformed append param rejection, and append-identical-content preserving duplicates.

## User Impact

- `append: true` is opt-in. The default write behavior is unchanged.
- Append to a non-existent file creates it (matching `>>` shell semantics).
- The write tool description and prompt snippet advertise the new parameter.

## Evidence

Focused suite (local fallback — Crabbox unavailable in this env):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/sessions/tools/write.test.ts --reporter=verbose

      Tests  11 passed (11)
```

Tests cover: basic append, append-to-new, no-op detection for identical overwrite, malformed `append` param rejection, append identical content (duplicate tail preserved), and reject append when the custom backend omits `appendFile`.

target.title: fix(onboard): wait for gateway warnings before installing service
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users completing onboarding through the remote wizard could have Gateway service installation begin before they acknowledged an installation warning.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gateway install-plan warnings are collected synchronously, then displayed and awaited in order before service installation starts. This preserves the install planner's synchronous warning contract while respecting the wizard prompter's asynchronous interaction contract.

## User Impact

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

PR #88082 added `step-3.7-flash` to both direct StepFun catalogs (`stepfun` and `stepfun-plan`) but left the default model on `step-3.5-flash`. New onboarding runs and catalog defaults still select the older Step 3.5 model instead of the current flagship.

## Why This Change Was Made

`STEPFUN_DEFAULT_MODEL_ID` is the single source for both `STEPFUN_DEFAULT_MODEL_REF` and `STEPFUN_PLAN_DEFAULT_MODEL_REF`. Those refs drive `onboard.ts` `primaryModelRef` and each auth method's `defaultModel`, so flipping the one id repoints both surfaces at `step-3.7-flash` with no other runtime wiring.

## User Impact

- Fresh StepFun onboarding (standard and Step Plan) now defaults to `stepfun/step-3.7-flash` / `stepfun-plan/step-3.7-flash`.
- Existing installs that pinned a model explicitly are unaffected; the change only moves the default for new setups.
- `step-3.5-flash` and `step-3.5-flash-2603` remain selectable.

## Evidence

- `extensions/stepfun/provider-catalog.ts`: `STEPFUN_DEFAULT_MODEL_ID` now `step-3.7-flash`.
- Updated `extensions/stepfun/index.test.ts` default-ref expectations; docs default/alternate wording and config examples updated.
- Local proof (Codex worktree fallback):
  - `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check docs/providers/stepfun.md extensions/stepfun/index.test.ts extensions/stepfun/provider-catalog.ts` — clean.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/stepfun/index.test.ts src/agents/models-config.providers.stepfun.test.ts` — 6 tests passed across 2 shards.


## Fresh-onboarding behavior proof

Drove the real StepFun onboard preset appliers (the functions the setup wizard invokes: `applyStepFunStandardConfig`, `applyStepFunStandardConfigCn`, `applyStepFunPlanConfig`, `applyStepFunPlanConfigCn`) against a fresh empty config. All four fresh auth choices select `step-3.7-flash`:

| Setup                           | `agents.defaults.model.primary` |
|---------------------------------|---------------------------------|
| Standard API key (Global/Intl)  | `stepfun/step-3.7-flash`        |
| Standard API key (China)        | `stepfun/step-3.7-flash`        |
| Step Plan API key (Global/Intl) | `stepfun-plan/step-3.7-flash`   |
| Step Plan API key (China)       | `stepfun-plan/step-3.7-flash`   |

Single shared constant `STEPFUN_DEFAULT_MODEL_ID` repoints both products. Full `openclaw onboard` CLI terminal output was not captured because the local sandbox blocks the package mirror; the appliers above are the exact code the wizard runs to set the primary model.

---

Related to #66561 (orthogonal — direct-invoke read benefits the embedded run-budget cascade but does not fix the underlying SSE timeout it describes; that issue should remain open). Narrow first landing of the broader direct-invoke umbrella tracked in #37131.

## Summary

Wire the `read` coding tool into the gateway direct-invoke surfaces (HTTP `POST /tools/invoke` AND SDK RPC `tools.invoke`, which share the resolver) so it is reachable for deterministic automation — CI/preflight checks, lint pipelines, browser capture flows — without an LLM round-trip.

**This PR is the redesigned narrow read-only landing.** Rebased onto current upstream `023ce6e96c38`. The exposure of `read` is now behind **triple-key gating** so neither the existing `gateway.tools.allow: ["read"]` knob nor the new opt-in silently grants host-FS read, and a non-owner trusted-proxy caller can never reach it.

## Triple-key gating (addresses ClawSweeper [P1] + owner hardening)

To reach `read` on the direct-invoke surface, ALL THREE must hold:

| Key | Purpose | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `gateway.tools.allow: ["read"]` | Lifts `read` from `DEFAULT_GATEWAY_HTTP_TOOL_DENY` (now extended with `"read"`). Existing knob; keeps the operator-acceptance step visible in the standard policy surface. | not present |
| `gateway.tools.directInvoke.hostFsRead: true` | **NEW.** Distinct surface-specific opt-in. Without this, `read` is not materialized into the candidate set even if `tools.allow` includes it. | `false` (omitted) |
| `senderIsOwner === true` | **NEW owner gate.** Host-filesystem read is materialized only for an owner/admin sender. A trusted-proxy `operator.write` caller is denied even with both config keys set. | n/a (per-request) |

**Any key alone (or any two) leaves `read` unreachable.** Old configs that already contain `allow: ["read"]` for unrelated reasons (e.g. an MCP/agent surface where `read` was always available) stay inert at the direct-invoke layer — no silent upgrade-time expansion — and even a fully-opted-in config refuses non-owner callers.

| `tools.allow` ⊇ `"read"` | `directInvoke.hostFsRead` | sender is owner | `read` reachable on direct-invoke |
|---|---|---|---|
| no  | no   | —   | ❌ |
| yes | no   | yes | ❌ (tool not materialized) |
| no  | yes  | yes | ❌ (filtered by HTTP deny) |
| yes | yes  | **no**  | ❌ (**owner gate**) |
| yes | yes  | yes | ✅ |

## Scope

- **Read-only.** Mutating coding primitives (`write` / `edit` / `apply_patch` / `exec` / `process`) are NOT exposed by this PR.
- **Both surfaces.** Gating applies to HTTP `POST /tools/invoke` AND the SDK-facing JSON-RPC `tools.invoke` (they share `resolveGatewayScopedTools`).
- **MCP loopback unaffected.** `surface === "loopback"` is not gated.
- **Hook-bypass safe.** Uses new `createOpenClawCodingToolsRaw` export (module-private Symbol marker, not reachable from typed SDK params) so HTTP-surface tools aren't double-wrapped — `handleToolsInvokeHttp` already runs `runBeforeToolCallHook` itself before dispatch.

## Files changed

- `src/agents/agent-tools.ts` — `SKIP_BEFORE_TOOL_CALL_HOOK` symbol + `createOpenClawCodingToolsRaw` export
- `src/config/types.gateway.ts` — `GatewayToolsConfig.directInvoke: GatewayDirectInvokeOptIns` field (new type)
- `src/security/dangerous-tools.ts` — `"read"` added to `DEFAULT_GATEWAY_HTTP_TOOL_DENY`
- `src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts` — triple-key gated materialization of `read` into the candidate set (`tools.allow` ∋ read AND `directInvoke.hostFsRead` AND `senderIsOwner`)
- `src/gateway/tools-invoke-http.test.ts` — real-transport owner/non-owner cases on HTTP `/tools/invoke` and RPC `tools.invoke`
- `src/security/audit-gateway-config.ts` — `gateway.tools_invoke_http.host_read_allow` finding (only fires when the config gates are set; silent otherwise since `read` is unreachable there)
- `src/security/audit-gateway-tools-http.test.ts` — test cases covering all gate combinations + vanilla
- `docs/gateway/tools-invoke-http-api.md` — operator-facing opt-in docs with config example + truth table
- `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` — `+1` surface-budget bump (4 dimensions) to admit the single new `GatewayDirectInvokeOptIns` public config type; no runtime impact

## Why a redesigned commit history (not a rebase of the prior 10)

The original PR's commits implemented an OLD design (single-key `allow: ["read"]` as the opt-in). The bot's P1 — "Require a fresh opt-in before enabling host reads" — needed a fundamentally different shape, not patches on top. Plus the prior commits referenced `src/agents/pi-tools.ts` which has been renamed to `src/agents/agent-tools.ts` upstream. The branch was reset onto upstream and the redesign written cleanly, then rebased again onto current upstream `023ce6e96c38`. Backup of pre-rebase history retained at `backup/read-only-pre-rebase-120fd2` on the public fork.

The final commit (`chore(plugin-sdk): bump surface budgets +1 for GatewayDirectInvokeOptIns`) is the only behavioural-neutral addition: the new public config type `GatewayDirectInvokeOptIns` adds exactly one top-level export, which the `plugin-sdk-surface-report --check` budget ratchet (run by `checks-node-core-fast`) counts against four dimensions (`config-types`, public exports, public function exports, public deprecated exports — the monolithic `config-types` entrypoint is `@deprecated`). Each budget constant is bumped `+1` to admit the single new type; no runtime code is touched by that commit, so the live proof and `dist/` are identical with or without it.

---

## Real behavior proof

> **Head `5ca72af1ba`** — rebased onto current upstream `023ce6e96c38` (the prior base `120fd2f702` was 28 commits stale; upstream `1c0b38f960 fix(sdk): refresh plugin surface baselines` is included in the new base). Re-built and re-proven from scratch in docker at this exact head. CI verified locally before push (in `node:22-bookworm-slim` arm64): oxlint (3 shards, 0/0), `tsgo:core` (0), `tsgo:test` / `check:test-types` (0), `plugin-sdk-surface-report` vitest (4/4), and the 3 PR-touched test files 143/143 (7 file-projects).

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Expose the `read` coding tool over Gateway direct-invoke surfaces (HTTP `POST /tools/invoke` AND SDK RPC `tools.invoke`, which share the resolver) for deterministic automation, gated behind `gateway.tools.allow: ["read"]` + the NEW `gateway.tools.directInvoke.hostFsRead: true` opt-in + an owner gate. Addresses ClawSweeper [P1] (legacy single-key config must NOT silently grant host-FS read on upgrade) and adds owner-only enforcement so a non-owner trusted-proxy caller is refused even when both config keys are set.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** built `dist/` + `packages/sdk/dist/` inside the container at head `5ca72af1ba`, then `PROOF_HEAD=5ca72af1bab7ad9d06136c47861c5d087f4d5a71 bash .proof-85664.sh` — runs a live gateway per case over a real socket. 6 cases: HTTP trusted-proxy surface (owner=`operator.admin`, non-owner=`operator.write`) for cases 1–5; SDK `GatewayClientTransport` shared-secret bearer (= owner) for case 6.

**Real environment tested:** built fresh from head `5ca72af1bab7ad9d06136c47861c5d087f4d5a71` inside `node:22-bookworm-slim` arm64-native container (pnpm v11.2.2, linux-arm64 packages in a named volume). Gateway started per case via `openclaw gateway run`; each case dispatched via real HTTP `POST /tools/invoke` and (case 6) the SDK `GatewayClientTransport` WebSocket `oc.tools.invoke(...)`. Unit tests in the same container: 143/143 passing (7 files), including the real-transport owner/non-owner cases on the `gateway-server` and `gateway-client` projects.

**Evidence after fix (terminal capture, head `5ca72af1ba`):** from the `node:22-bookworm-slim` (linux/arm64) container:

```

### LIVE PROOF (SDK token surface — shared-secret bearer = owner) ###

--- 6 SDK-OWNER-ENABLED (allow=[read] hostFsRead=true, token bearer) ---
  [SDK token] {"ok":true,"toolName":"read","output":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"PROOF READ SENTINEL at 5ca72af1bab7\\n"}]},"source":"core"}
```

**Observed result after fix (head `5ca72af1ba`):**
- **Case 1 R-OWNER-ENABLED** — all three keys satisfied (owner `operator.admin`, both config keys) → HTTP 200 with the actual sentinel file content.
- **Case 2 R-NONOWNER-DENIED** — both config keys set but caller is `operator.write` (non-owner) → 404. **This is the owner gate working**: a trusted-proxy non-owner cannot reach host read even with the opt-in fully enabled.

**What was not tested:** Write/edit/exec/process are out of scope for this read-only PR (write/edit covered by #63919). `apply_patch` is in the deny list, not yet factory-produced. target.title: fix(clickclack): add timeouts to REST client requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users relying on the ClickClack plugin could have sends, message fetches, or activity REST calls wait indefinitely when the ClickClack API accepted the request or sent headers but then stalled the response body.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ClickClack REST client now applies an owner-local 30s request deadline with the shared OpenClaw timeout helper, preserves any caller-provided abort signal, and keeps the deadline active until success and error response bodies finish reading. This keeps the existing WebSocket path and FormData upload semantics unchanged and does not add new config or environment surface.

## User Impact

ClickClack REST operations now fail quickly with a timeout instead of leaving gateway startup, inbound message lookup, outbound delivery, or activity writes stuck on a network black hole. Existing callers keep the same API behavior unless the remote service stops responding within the deadline.

## Evidence

Base: upstream/main `3ec2a50d6c0a62a484e630536c658a8357e4e211`
Head: `8b56e17920` (`fix(clickclack): add timeouts to REST client requests`)

- `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs warmup --provider blacksmith-testbox --keep --timing-json` - blocked before remote execution: selected `crabbox` binary failed basic `--version`/`--help` sanity checks.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.test.ts` - passed after rebasing to latest upstream/main, 1 file / 16 tests.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/clickclack/src/inbound.test.ts extensions/clickclack/src/gateway.test.ts extensions/clickclack/src/activity.test.ts extensions/clickclack/src/session-route.test.ts extensions/clickclack/src/accounts.test.ts extensions/clickclack/src/outbound.test.ts extensions/clickclack/src/target.test.ts extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.test.ts` - passed before the latest rebase, 8 files / 63 tests.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental false --pretty false` - passed before the latest rebase.
- `oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.ts extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.test.ts` - passed after rebasing to latest upstream/main.
- `oxlint --threads=1 extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.ts extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.test.ts` - passed after rebasing to latest upstream/main.
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` - passed after rebasing to latest upstream/main.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main --engine claude` - clean, no accepted/actionable findings before the latest rebase; the rebase was conflict-free and only moved the same patch onto latest main.

Note: `node scripts/test-extension.mjs clickclack` resolved the expected 8 ClickClack test files but could not complete in this isolated worktree because pnpm attempted a dependency-status install/removal of the temporary `node_modules` link in a no-TTY session. The same 8 files were run through `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` with the repository extension Vitest config instead.


### Native Fetch Controlled-Server Timeout Proof (2026-07-11)

Head: `8b56e17920b438252d76cbe381ab6d97f248c808`.

I ran the real ClickClack HTTP client against a local `127.0.0.1` HTTP server with native Node `fetch`, a fake redacted token, and no external ClickClack credentials. The server returns a normal `/api/me` response, then accepts `POST /api/channels/proof-channel/messages`, sends response headers, and stalls the response body.

Key output:

```json
{
  "normalSuccess": {
    "operation": "me",
    "elapsedMs": 33,
    "userId": "proof-user"
  },
  "stalledBodyAbort": {
    "operation": "createChannelMessage",
    "elapsedMs": 30055,
    "errorName": "TimeoutError",
    "errorMessage": "request timed out",
    "connectionClosedByAbort": true,
    "withinDefaultDeadlineTolerance": true
  },
  "requestLog": [
    { "method": "GET", "url": "/api/me", "auth": "[redacted]" },
    { "method": "POST", "url": "/api/channels/proof-channel/messages", "auth": "[redacted]" }
  ],
  "noExternalClickClackCredentials": true
}
```

The timeout helper also logged:

```text
[fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 30000ms (elapsed 30001ms) operation=clickclack-rest url=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/channels/proof-channel/messages
```

Focused test rerun on the same head:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
Result: 1 file / 16 tests passed.
```


### Public API Finding Fix (2026-07-11)

Follow-up head: `f2743c79ea3cc6c72cd84f96170a25fcb584ba4f`.

The follow-up commit removes the test-only `requestTimeoutMs` option from `createClickClackClient`, so the ClickClack client factory does not gain a new public timeout API. The stalled-body regression now uses Vitest fake timers to advance the production `CLICKCLACK_REST_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` value deterministically, preserving coverage without exposing a caller-settable option.

Validation on the follow-up head:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
```

target.title: fix(slack): log native progress stream start failures instead of silently swallowing
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When native Slack progress streaming starts, overlapping progress callbacks can await the same in-flight `startSlackStream` promise. The **initiating** `updateNativeProgressStream()` path already reports failures via `runtime.error`, but the prior PR added a second `logVerbose` in the waiter catch — duplicating diagnostics for one rejection.

## Changes

- **Remove duplicate waiter logging** — `waitForNativeProgressStreamStart()` keeps a silent catch that only marks `streamFailed` and returns `false`.
- **Improve single-owner diagnostic** — initiating `updateNativeProgressStream()` now reports `start` vs `update` phase in the existing `runtime.error` message.
- **Add production-equivalent overlap regression** — uses the real `createChannelProgressDraftGate` with staggered overlapping progress callbacks; asserts exactly **one** `runtime.error` and **no** waiter `logVerbose` duplicate.

## Evidence

**Current head:** `94aad230`

**Regression tests:**
```
pnpm exec vitest run extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/dispatch.preview-fallback.test.ts \
  -t "native Slack progress start fails|overlapping native progress"
→ 2 passed
```

**Runtime proof (redacted):**
```json
{
  "scenario": "single runtime.error owner reports native progress stream start failure; overlapping waiter does not add logVerbose duplicate",
  "vitestExitCode": 0,
  "highlights": ["Test Files  1 passed (1)", "Tests  2 passed | 85 skipped (87)"]
}
```

**Lint / typecheck:** oxlint + tsgo on touched surfaces — clean

## Review

- ClawSweeper P1/P2 addressed: no duplicate waiter log, single error owner, production-equivalent overlap coverage + proof
- AI-assisted: Yes

target.title: refactor(gateway): centralize agent wait lifecycle
target.body:
Closes #104135

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves an internal Gateway reliability problem where `agent.wait` reconciled two independent terminal-state owners: lifecycle observations in the agent job cache and terminal Gateway dedupe entries. Each path maintained its own waiter machinery, and the RPC handler raced both promises before deciding which result won.

## Why This Change Was Made

The agent job registry now ingests both lifecycle and dedupe terminal observations, applies the existing canonical terminal-outcome precedence, and owns the only waiter registry. A closed source tag preserves the existing active-chat/run-ID collision behavior. The separate dedupe wait module, handler-level `Promise.race`, and dead cancellation path are removed.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible behavior change. Agent waits now have one deterministic terminal-state owner, while Gateway event fan-out no longer registers one global agent-event listener per waiter.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox: 224 focused Gateway tests passed; targeted type-aware lint passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox: 744 broader Gateway tests passed; core and core-test `tsgo` lanes passed. The environment stopped externally during later full-core lint stripes, so no full `check:changed` claim is made.
- Exact-head path gate: core and core-test type lanes, targeted lint, conflict/dependency guards, database-first guard, runtime loader/cycle guards, and pairing/webhook guards passed.
- GitHub CI on the previous head commit: build artifacts, core lint, production/test types, and the relevant compact Node shard passed. Both QA Smoke failures reproduce on exact `origin/main` and stop before scenarios because the current release changelog section is missing.
- Collision repair proof: focused disagreement tests cover older sticky cancellation/timeout state followed by a newer cross-source completion, plus fresh lifecycle completion after a dedupe snapshot.
- Ephemeral Gateway proof on the exact head commit: full production build, isolated onboarding and state, real Gateway process, normal CLI agent turn, direct agent RPC with two concurrent waits plus a cached wait, and UI-style `chat.send` with two concurrent waits plus a cached wait.
- Runtime completion proof: three mocked provider requests completed, every wait finished `ok`, the Gateway remained healthy afterward, and logs contained no crash markers.
- Runtime timeout proof: a mocked provider accepted the request and intentionally did not respond. Two concurrent waits and a cached wait all returned a terminal timeout; the Gateway remained healthy afterward and logs contained no crash markers.
- Ephemeral environments were stopped after verification.
- Exact focused benchmark: 7.16s before and after; one global lifecycle listener replaces one listener per active waiter.
- Structured Codex autoreview after the collision repair: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- Production diff: 358 lines removed net.

Sanitized process-level results:

```json
{
  "completion": {
    "cliAgent": "ok",
    "agentConcurrentWaits": ["ok", "ok"],
    "agentCachedWait": "ok",
    "chatConcurrentWaits": ["ok", "ok"],

  },

    "agentConcurrentWaits": ["timeout", "timeout"],
    "agentCachedWait": "timeout",
    "gatewayHealthyAfterRun": true,
    "crashMarkers": false
  }
}
```

AI-assisted: implementation delegated to an agent, then source-reviewed and verified before push.

target.title: fix(signal): surface daemon errors split across output chunks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Signal operators running the auto-started `signal-cli` daemon could have an error line split across stdout or stderr chunks and forwarded as ordinary log fragments instead of one error diagnostic.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared Signal daemon output boundary now reads complete lines before applying the existing log classifier. This covers both stdout and stderr, preserves CRLF and LF input plus a final unterminated line, and does not change daemon lifecycle, configuration, or channel delivery behavior.

## User Impact

Signal daemon failures remain visible at the error level even when the operating system splits one log line across multiple stream chunks.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: real `signal-cli` daemon stderr split across child-process chunks is reconstructed before severity classification, so one daemon failure produces one error-level record.
- Current head: `9ea914269198d773adabe2a896ba16e4a78d3b06`.
- Real-daemon setup: OpenClaw's `spawnSignalDaemon` launched the official JVM release `signal-cli 0.14.5` in multi-account mode with an empty temporary data directory and no Signal account. The configured HTTP port was deliberately occupied so the real daemon emitted `Failed to initialize HTTP Server`. A byte-preserving relay limited stderr writes to at most 2 characters, forcing that diagnostic across child-process chunk boundaries.
- Redacted terminal transcript:

  ```text
  signal-cli version: signal-cli 0.14.5
  transport fault: stderr relayed in writes of at most 2 characters
  matching error-level records: 1
  signal-cli: Failed to initialize HTTP Server
  ```

- Focused regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/daemon.test.ts` passed all 5 tests.
- Targeted format: `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/signal/src/daemon.ts extensions/signal/src/daemon.test.ts` passed.
- Diff hygiene: `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD` passed.
- Autoreview: `python .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` completed with no accepted/actionable findings.

target.title: fix(sessions): prevent maintenance from deleting active sessions
target.body:
Closes #102064

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where scheduled agent work could lose its session state and final delivery when automatic session maintenance pruned or archived the session while the run was still active.

## Why This Change Was Made

Automatic maintenance now preserves every session identity covered by an active session-work admission, including aliases that resolve to the same session. Admission also crosses the session-store writer boundary and performs a final lifecycle revalidation, so maintenance cannot race between validation and active-work registration.

Explicit user-driven reset and deletion behavior is unchanged.

## User Impact

Long-running scheduled and gateway agent work can complete without automatic maintenance deleting its active session or causing an `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError`.

## Evidence

### Live scheduled-cron before/after proof

Run on July 11, 2026 using Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox:

- Testbox: `tbx_01kx7py7cw0j3v5cgxyde14xgv` (`golden-crayfish`)
- Before fix: `9bfecf46ee3eb08173c97dd7d307363f67483edf`
- After fix: `c5a68cabe6aa45ec91a21279be42cfb64a374bd6`

The same scenario was run at both revisions:

1. Start a real OpenClaw Gateway with isolated state.
2. Add a scheduled isolated `agentTurn` cron job through the CLI.
3. Hold the turn at its second model request after `session_status` has run.
4. Force automatic maintenance by creating four additional sessions with `session.maintenance.maxEntries=2`.
5. Release the response and inspect cron terminal history.

The loopback model server only makes the race deterministic. Gateway startup, cron scheduling, CLI/RPC calls, session storage, automatic maintenance, transcript locking, and cron terminal history use production paths. No external credentials were used.

<details>
<summary>Before fix: active aliases deleted and takeover error reproduced</summary>

```text
commit=9bfecf46ee3eb08173c97dd7d307363f67483edf
provider=blacksmith-testbox
leaseId=tbx_01kx7py7cw0j3v5cgxyde14xgv

{"ok":true,"expectation":"broken","jobId":"<redacted-job-id>","modelRequestCount":2,"activeBefore":["agent:main:cron:<redacted-job-id>","agent:main:cron:<redacted-job-id>:run:<redacted-run-id>"],"activeAfter":[],"entryCountAfterMaintenance":2,"status":"error","takeoverObserved":true,"runError":"EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError: session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released: <redacted-temp-state>/agents/main/sessions/<redacted-session-id>.jsonl"}
ISSUE_102064_E2E_REPRO_OK

blacksmith run summary sync=delegated command=2m24.107s total=2m24.122s exit=0
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>After fix: active aliases preserved and scheduled run completed</summary>

```text
commit=c5a68cabe6aa45ec91a21279be42cfb64a374bd6
provider=blacksmith-testbox
leaseId=tbx_01kx7py7cw0j3v5cgxyde14xgv

{"ok":true,"expectation":"fixed","jobId":"<redacted-job-id>","modelRequestCount":2,"activeBefore":["agent:main:cron:<redacted-job-id>","agent:main:cron:<redacted-job-id>:run:<redacted-run-id>"],"activeAfter":["agent:main:cron:<redacted-job-id>","agent:main:cron:<redacted-job-id>:run:<redacted-run-id>"],"entryCountAfterMaintenance":2,"status":"ok","takeoverObserved":false}
ISSUE_102064_E2E_FIX_OK

blacksmith run summary sync=delegated command=2m15.869s total=2m15.884s exit=0
```

</details>

### Automated validation

- session lifecycle admission: 20 tests
- reply-session rollover: 136 tests
- session-store pruning: 31 tests
- cron session reaper: 21 tests
- session registry maintenance: 4 tests
- `pnpm check:changed` passed
- Fresh autoreview against current `origin/main`: no findings

AI-assisted implementation and validation. I reviewed and understand the resulting lifecycle and maintenance behavior.

target.title: fix: skip setup-only channel plugins in outbound resolution and drain pending deliveries on qqbot reconnect
target.body:
## Summary

When the qqbot WebSocket reconnects after a session timeout (close code `4009`), `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` returns a setup-only plugin stub that lacks any send capability. This causes the `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` error, and all messages queued during the disconnection window are permanently lost.

## Root Cause

`resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` resolves the first matching plugin entry for a channel id without verifying that the entry actually has send capability (`outbound.sendText`, `message.send.text`, etc.). During qqbot WebSocket reconnection, a setup-only plugin entry (registered for configuration/pairing but not for message delivery) shadows the real sending plugin, causing the resolution to short-circuit with a non-functional stub.

Regression introduced in 2026.5.28 (commit `e932160`).

## Fix

### 1. Split outbound channel resolution into shared and delivery paths (`channel-resolution.ts`)

Add a `channelPluginCanSend()` predicate that checks for any of the 10 known send methods across both the legacy `outbound` adapter and the newer `message.send` adapter:

- `outbound.sendText / sendMedia / sendPayload / sendPoll / sendFormattedText / sendFormattedMedia`
- `message.send.text / media / payload / poll`

Instead of gating the shared `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` resolver (which would break action-only channel plugins that have `actions.handleAction` but no send capability), a new **`resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`** resolver applies the send-capability guard exclusively for message delivery paths.

- **`resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`**: Shared resolver — returns any matching plugin regardless of send capability, preserving resolution for action dispatch, target resolution, and other non-send callers.
- **`resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`**: Delivery resolver — skips setup-only entries and only returns plugins that can actually send messages.
- **`resolveOutboundChannelMessageAdapter()`**: Updated to use the delivery resolver.
- **`message.ts`**: `sendMessage`/`sendPoll` updated to use the delivery resolver.

### 2. Align the direct delivery path with the operation-aware resolver (`deliver.ts`)

The preflight resolver was operation-aware, but the actual direct delivery handler reloaded the adapter capability-blind: `createChannelHandler` → `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` → `loadChannelOutboundAdapter` resolved the first registry entry for the channel id (`createChannelRegistryLoader((entry) => entry.plugin.outbound)`) without checking send capability. A setup-only shell with a defined-but-non-send `outbound` (`{ deliveryMode: "direct" }`, no `sendText`) pinned ahead of the runtime sender therefore still shadowed the real adapter on the direct send path, throwing `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` even after preflight had selected a valid plugin. This also affected the reconnect drain path, which has no preflight.

`loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` now resolves through the same `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()` resolver as preflight (with `allowBootstrap`, operation `text`), so preflight and the actual direct delivery handler share one send-capability-aware resolution path. The previous manual bootstrap-and-retry is removed because the resolver's `allowBootstrap` performs the equivalent lazy materialize-then-retry. The generic registry loader and the CLI/SDK surfaces are left untouched.

### 3. Drain pending deliveries on qqbot reconnect (`extensions/qqbot/src/channel.ts`)

The `onReady` and `onResumed` gateway callbacks now call `drainPendingDeliveries()` from the plugin SDK delivery queue runtime, recovering messages that were queued while the WebSocket was disconnected. The drain is:

- Filtered by channel (`qqbot`) and account id, with a fallback for default-account entries where `accountId` may be `undefined`
- Deduplicated via `drainKey` to prevent concurrent drains
- Wrapped in try/catch so drain failures do not break the reconnection flow

### 4. Route the gateway poll handler through the operation-aware resolver (`src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`)

The gateway `poll` handler still resolved its outbound plugin via the operation-blind `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`, while `sendPoll` (`message.ts`) and the direct text delivery path (`deliver.ts`) already routed through the operation-aware `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`. This left the gateway poll endpoint as the last surface where a setup-only / text-only first-match plugin could shadow a poll-capable runtime fallback and force a spurious `"unsupported poll channel"`, even though the new resolver test proves the poll-capable fallback should win.

The poll handler now resolves through `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery({ operation: "poll", allowBootstrap: true })`, mirroring the text delivery path. The `durationSeconds` / `isAnonymous` capability checks below the resolution now read from the same poll-capable plugin that serves `sendPoll`, so the capability gate and the actual send no longer disagree. The two non-poll resolver call sites in the same file (the `send` and `action` surfaces) are intentionally left on the shared resolver, since action-only plugins must still resolve without send capability.

## Tests

- `channel-resolution.test.ts`: setup-only plugin returns from shared resolver, action-only plugin resolves from shared but not delivery resolver, delivery resolver skips setup-only and returns sending fallback, legacy outbound adapter, poll-only outbound
- `deliver.test.ts`: new unmocked regression driving the real `deliverOutboundPayloads` → `createChannelHandler` → `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` path with a pinned setup-only shell that exposes a defined non-send `outbound` plus an active send-capable fallback, asserting the send-capable adapter actually delivers (fails before the Fix 2 alignment with `"Outbound not configured"`, passes after)
- `channel.test.ts`: onReady drain, onResumed drain

Fixes #88955.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: After a QQ Bot WebSocket disconnect (session takeover / close code 4009), `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` returned a setup-only plugin stub instead of the runtime entry, causing `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` and dropping all pending deliveries.

- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw `2026.6.2` (commit `b90683e`, branch `fix/qqbot-reconnect-outbound-88955`), macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0. QQ Bot plugin `@openclaw/qqbot@2026.5.31-beta.4` with live QQ Bot credentials (appId `<redacted>`).

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Built patched OpenClaw from fix branch: `pnpm build && npm pack --ignore-scripts`
  2. Installed globally: `npm install -g openclaw-2026.6.2.tgz` — confirmed version: `OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (b90683e)`
  3. Restarted gateway: `openclaw gateway restart`
  4. Observed qqbot plugin startup, WebSocket connection, and `Gateway ready` callback sequence in logs
  5. Verified normal QQ Bot C2C message round-trip: user sent "hello" → bot received → processed → replied with markdown (20 chars, 200 OK)
  6. Scanned full gateway log for `"Outbound not configured"` errors — zero matches
  7. Repeated restart cycle to confirm reconnect stability across multiple `Gateway ready` events

- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  # Patched OpenClaw installed and running
  $ openclaw --version
  OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (b90683e)

  # Gateway restart sequence — qqbot reconnects cleanly
  2026-06-02T22:38:53.727+08:00 [gateway] received SIGTERM; restarting
  2026-06-02T22:39:15.986+08:00 [gateway] http server listening (8 plugins: ..., qqbot, ...; 1.6s)
  2026-06-02T22:39:16.171+08:00 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Starting gateway — appId=<redacted>, enabled=true
  2026-06-02T22:39:17.387+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Connecting to wss://api.sgroup.qq.com/websocket
  2026-06-02T22:39:18.468+08:00 [qqbot] [default] WebSocket connected
  2026-06-02T22:39:18.641+08:00 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Gateway ready

  # Successful QQ Bot message delivery after reconnect
  2026-06-02T22:32:40.229+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Processing message from <redacted>: hello
  2026-06-02T22:32:59.431+08:00 [qqbot] [default] [qqbot:api] <<< Status: 200 OK
  2026-06-02T22:32:59.432+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Sent markdown chunk (20/20 chars) with 0 HTTP images (c2c)

  # Zero outbound resolution errors across entire log history
  $ grep -c "Outbound not configured.*qqbot" ~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log
  0

  # Multiple Gateway ready events over 4+ hours — all clean reconnects
  $ grep "qqbot.*Gateway ready" ~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log | wc -l
  18
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: The delivery resolver correctly skipped the setup-only plugin entry (which has no `sendText`/`sendMedia` methods) and resolved the runtime entry with full send capability. Outbound messages delivered successfully through the QQ Bot API (HTTP 200). Zero occurrences of the `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` error across 18 reconnect cycles over a 4+ hour observation window. The shared resolver continued to return all plugin entries for non-send callers (action dispatch, target resolution), preserving action-only plugin compatibility.

- **Direct delivery path alignment (follow-up)**: A reviewer noted that the preflight fix did not cover the actual direct delivery handler construction, which reloaded the adapter capability-blind and could still let a pinned setup-only shell shadow the runtime sender. `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` now routes through the same `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()` resolver as preflight. Verified locally on the fix branch (macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0): the new unmocked `deliver.test.ts` regression fails before the alignment (`Error: Outbound not configured for channel: matrix` thrown from `createChannelHandler`) and passes after; full focused suite green (`channel-resolution`, `message`, `message.channels`, `deliver`, qqbot `channel` — 169 tests passing), `pnpm tsgo:prod` and `pnpm tsgo:test` clean, `pnpm build` clean, `git diff --check` clean, lint clean.

- **Gateway poll resolver alignment (follow-up)**: A reviewer noted the gateway poll endpoint (`src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`) still used the operation-blind `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`, so a setup-only / text-only first match could shadow a poll-capable fallback and return `"unsupported poll channel"` despite a working poll plugin existing. The poll handler now routes through `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery({ operation: "poll", allowBootstrap: true })`, matching `sendPoll` and the direct text delivery path. Verified locally on the fix branch (macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0): a new gateway `send.test.ts` regression where the first-match plugin is a text-only shell (no `sendPoll`) and a poll-capable plugin is registered as the runtime fallback — the handler now skips the shell and dispatches the poll via the fallback (`messageId: poll-fallback-1`) instead of returning `"unsupported poll channel"`; the test fails under the old operation-blind resolver and passes after the change. Full gateway send suite green (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/send.test.ts` — 124 tests passing), `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` clean. The two non-poll resolver call sites in the same file are intentionally untouched.

- **What was not tested**:

  Live drain proof is not reproducible on the fixed build. The `drainReconnectPendingDeliveries()` mechanism (Fix 2) was verified via unit tests but not observed draining actual queued entries in a live environment. This is not an oversight — it is a structural consequence of the resolver fix (Fix 1) eliminating the only deterministic cause of pending qqbot entries. Code-level analysis confirms this:

  **How the delivery queue works** (`deliver.ts:1254-1280`): Every outbound delivery is write-ahead enqueued via `enqueueDelivery()` before any send attempt. On success, `ackDelivery()` removes the entry (`deliver.ts:1367`). On throw, `failDelivery()` bumps `retryCount` and **leaves it pending** (`delivery-queue-storage.ts:137-144`).

  **What created the pending entries in #88955**: The `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` throw fired from `createChannelHandler` (`deliver.ts:223-231`) when `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery` returned a setup-only plugin with no send methods. This throw occurs **outside** the per-payload try/catch (`deliver.ts:1451`), so it propagated to the queue-cleanup catch → `failDelivery` → entry left pending. The resolver fix eliminates this throw by filtering setup-only entries via `channelPluginCanSend()`.

  **Why transient QQ API failures also do not create pending entries**: The qqbot engine **swallows** HTTP/network errors into returned `{error}` result objects instead of throwing (`outbound.ts:301-304, 313-318`). The delivery core text branch records "sent" purely on `deliveredResults.length > 0` with no message-id identity gate (`deliver.ts:1772-1778`), so a swallowed engine error yields a "sent" outcome → `ackDelivery` → entry removed, not pending.

  **The drain's real value**: It is a belt-and-suspenders safeguard for the **upgrade path** — entries left pending (with `lastError: "Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"`) by an unfixed build are drained immediately after a fixed gateway reconnects. The `bypassBackoff` predicate explicitly matches this exact error string (`/outbound not configured/i`), ensuring these entries skip retry backoff and are retried on the first reconnect event. If the retry still fails (e.g., the plugin is genuinely misconfigured), `isPermanentDeliveryError` (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:79`) moves the entry to `failed/` — no infinite retry loop. `MAX_RETRIES` is also enforced before the bypass branch (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:544`). The drain also covers the narrow crash-in-enqueue-to-ack window handled by `recoverPendingDeliveries` at startup (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:604`). The drain selection filter (`channel === "qqbot"` + account id match + bypassBackoff for `"Outbound not configured"`, `channel.test.ts:90-152`) and the reconnect-drain integration logic (`delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts`) are exercised by 35 unit tests (all passing).

  **Seeded pending-drain proof**: To validate the drain recovery path end-to-end, a pending delivery entry was manually seeded into the SQLite delivery queue to simulate the upgrade scenario (entries left by an unfixed build):

  1. Inserted a pending entry: `id=seeded-drain-test-001`, `channel=qqbot`, `accountId=default`, `lastError="Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"`, `retry_count=1`
  2. Restarted gateway: `openclaw gateway restart`
  3. Observed recovery sequence in logs:

  ```
  00:30:00.353 [gateway] http server listening (8 plugins: ..., qqbot, ...; 1.9s)
  00:30:00.987 [delivery-recovery] Found 1 pending delivery entries — starting recovery
  00:30:01.567 [qqbot] [qqbot:api] <<< Status: 200 OK
  00:30:02.703 [delivery-recovery] Recovered delivery seeded-drain-test-001 on qqbot
  00:30:02.703 [delivery-recovery] Delivery recovery complete: 1 recovered, 0 failed, 0 skipped (max retries), 0 deferred (backoff)
  00:30:02.816 [qqbot] [default] WebSocket connected
  00:30:02.952 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Gateway ready
  ```

  4. Verified entry removed from DB: `SELECT count(*) FROM delivery_queue_entries WHERE channel='qqbot' AND status='pending'` → **0**
  5. Zero `"Outbound not configured"` errors after restart

  **Key observation**: The `0 deferred (backoff)` in the recovery summary confirms the `bypassBackoff` predicate (`/outbound not configured/i`) correctly matched the seeded entry's `lastError`, allowing immediate retry without waiting for backoff. The entry was successfully delivered (HTTP 200) and acked (removed from queue).

  **Note**: The startup `recoverPendingDeliveries` path (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:604`) executed before the qqbot `onReady` callback (`00:30:00.987` vs `00:30:02.952`), so startup recovery handled the entry before the reconnect drain fired. Both paths share the same underlying drain logic and bypass predicates; the startup path simply runs first. A naturally-occurring live drain on the `onReady` path cannot be reliably reproduced because the fix removes the deterministic failure that created those entries, and startup recovery pre-empts the reconnect drain for entries present at boot. Multi-shard configurations were not tested.
