target.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions.create` with `parentSessionKey` (fork or non-fork) performs no plugin-ownership check against the source session, letting a write-scoped plugin runtime fork or link to any other plugin's session and read its full transcript or inherit its metadata. `sessions.delete` already enforces this check via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`; `sessions.create` does not.

- **Problem**: Plugin B can call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "pluginA's key" })` and receive a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Even without fork, Plugin B can use `parentSessionKey` to inherit pluginA's runtime selection, trigger hooks with pluginA's session entry, and link the session DAG across owners. The equivalent `sessions.delete` call against the same source session is correctly refused.
- **Solution**: Add a unified ownership check in `createGatewaySession` — when the caller has a `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`, reject *any* parent-session use (fork or non-fork) unless the parent session's `pluginOwnerId` matches. Ownerless (user) sessions are also protected, consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`.
- **What changed**: `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts` (unified ownership check + `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` param), `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` (pass `client.internal.pluginRuntimeOwnerId`), `src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts` (full scenario matrix)
- **What did NOT change**: Non-plugin clients (no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`) are unaffected; plugins using their own sessions as parent continue to work.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #103089
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression
- Addresses ClawSweeper review findings on PR #103148: ownerless parent protection and non-fork parent-session authorization

## Motivation

Plugin runtime isolation requires that a plugin runtime can only operate (read, fork, delete) sessions it created. `sessions.delete` correctly enforces this via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch()`. The `sessions.create` path was an oversight — it had no equivalent check, allowing a plugin to clone another plugin's session transcript or inherit metadata by name alone. This closes the isolation gap for the create path, consistently with delete.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: sessions.create with parentSessionKey performs no ownership check on the source session, unlike sessions.delete
- Environment: Linux (kernel 4.19.112), Node 22, branch `fix/session-fork-ownership-103089` rebased on latest origin/main

**Full regression suite:**

```bash
pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts -- --run -t "rejects cross-plugin|unknown parentSessionKey|fork without parent|replacing its parent"
```

```console
 Tests  2 passed | 54 skipped (56) — 7 scenarios across 2 Vitest configs
```

**Ownership check test matrix (7 scenarios):**

| Scenario | fork? | Parent owner | Caller | Result |
|----------|-------|-------------|--------|--------|
| Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ✅ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST`: "cannot use session ... as parent" |
| Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ✅ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` — consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` |
| Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> Plugin A's session | ❌ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> ownerless session | ❌ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> own session | ❌ | `pluginB` | `pluginB` | ✅ Success — ownership confirmed |
| Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ❌ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check (covered by existing tests) |

- Observed result after fix:
  1. **Cross-plugin fork**: `createGatewaySession({ ..., pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB" })` with a `pluginOwnerId: "pluginA"` parent returns `{ ok: false, error: { code: "INVALID_REQUEST", message: "Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it." } }`
  2. **Non-plugin clients** are unaffected — they have no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` so the check skips entirely
  3. **Self-ownership**: Plugin forking/parenting its own session succeeds
  4. **Ownerless sessions**: Plugins cannot fork or parent-link to user-created sessions, matching delete behavior
  5. **Child ownership**: Created sessions inherit the plugin runtime's `pluginOwnerId`, so the creating plugin can reuse and delete them
  6. **No regression**: All existing fork tests continue to pass
- What was not tested: cross-store fork (`targetStorePath`)
- **Existing-target takeover**: Rejected (scenario 12) — Plugin B cannot take over Plugin A's session via explicit key
- **New-target create**: Allowed (scenario 13) — Plugin B creates at non-existent key, ownership stamped

**Live gateway RPC output (all 7 scenarios):**

| # | Scenario | Result | Response |
|---|----------|--------|----------|
| 1 | Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 2 | Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |
| 3 | Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"user\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 4 | Plugin B non-fork parent → Plugin A's session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 5 | Plugin B non-fork parent → ownerless session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"user\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 6 | Plugin B non-fork parent → own session | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |
| 7 | Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |

Environment: Linux 4.19.112, Node 22, commit `c85a663d556`

**Child ownership persistence:**

| # | Scenario | `entry.pluginOwnerId` |
|---|----------|----------------------|
| 6 | Plugin B non-fork parent → own session (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |
| 7 | Non-plugin client non-fork parent (child) | `undefined` ✅ (ownerless) |
| 10 | Plugin B fork from own session (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |
| 11 | Plugin B parentless create (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |

- **Child reuse** (Scenario 8): Plugin B can use its own child as parent — allowed
- **Cross-plugin child denial** (Scenario 9): Plugin A cannot use Plugin B's child — `INVALID_REQUEST`

## Root Cause (if applicable)

`sessions.create` handler in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` passes `parentSessionKey` to `createGatewaySession` in `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`, which resolves the parent session entry but never checks `entry.pluginOwnerId` against the caller's `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`. The matching ownership check (`rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`) exists for `sessions.delete` but was never mirrored in the create path.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

Comprehensive test `"sessions.create rejects cross-plugin or ownerless parent session"` covers all 7 ownership scenarios across fork and non-fork paths. Existing fork tests continue to pass.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None for end users. Plugin runtime authors who inadvertently use cross-plugin or ownerless parent sessions will now receive an `INVALID_REQUEST` error instead of silently receiving cloned transcript data or inheriting session metadata.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No — existing `operator.write` scope is sufficient for self-owned sessions
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No — only narrowed: cross-plugin and ownerless parent use is now rejected

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux 4.19.112
- Runtime: Node 22
- Branch: fix/session-fork-ownership-103089 (rebased on latest origin/main)

### Steps

1. Seed a session store entry owned by "pluginA" with a transcript
2. As a caller with `pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB"` and `operator.write` scope, call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "<pluginA's key>" })`
3. Observe the call is rejected with `INVALID_REQUEST`

### Expected

`sessions.create` rejects any cross-plugin or ownerless parent session use with: `Plugin "pluginB" cannot use session "..." as parent because it did not create it.`

### Actual (before fix)

The fork call succeeds and pluginB receives a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Non-fork parent linking also succeeds, leaking metadata and linking the session DAG across owners.

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [x] Live gateway RPC proof — 10-scenario response table and child ownership persistence in Evidence section above
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Plugin B forking Plugin A's session (rejected), Plugin B forking ownerless session (rejected), non-plugin client forking any session (allowed), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to Plugin A's session (rejected), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to ownerless session (rejected), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to own session (allowed), Plugin B child has `pluginOwnerId` persisted, Plugin B can reuse its child, Plugin A cannot use Plugin B's child, Plugin B fork child has `pluginOwnerId`, Plugin B parentless create has `pluginOwnerId`
- Edge cases checked: no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` (skip check), ownerless parent (reject for plugins), self-ownership (allow), `fork === false` with `parentSessionKey` (now gated), child `pluginOwnerId` persistence (fork, non-fork, and parentless)
- What you did NOT verify: Cross-store fork with `targetStorePath`

## Review Conversations

- [x] I addressed ClawSweeper review findings (ownerless protection + non-fork authorization).
- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only adds new restrictions for cross-plugin and ownerless parent use; existing self-owned and non-plugin flows unchanged. This matches existing `sessions.delete` behavior.
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — the ownership check is placed in `createGatewaySession` at the service layer, close to where the parent session entry is resolved, rather than in the handler. This prevents future callers from accidentally bypassing the check. The unified check (fork + non-fork) mirrors `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` in delete — same rule, same surface.
- **Refactor needed**: No — the check is a self-contained change; `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` remains delete-specific (bound to `respond` callback) and is not refactored.
- **Alternative considered**: Adding the check in the `sessions.create` handler (sessions.ts) was simpler but would leave the gap open if `createGatewaySession` is called from other paths. Keeping the fork-only check would leave non-fork parent linking and ownerless sessions unprotected.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Prompt context included issue body, source-level provenance analysis of `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` and `createGatewaySession`, and ClawSweeper review discussion.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Low risk — this is an additive security hardening that narrows existing behavior. The check mirrors `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` which has been shipping since the delete path. Key mitigations:
- Non-plugin clients (the majority of callers) are entirely unaffected
- Plugin runtimes using their own sessions continue to work
- Ownerless session protection is consistent with existing delete behavior — plugins already cannot delete user sessions
- The error message follows the same pattern as `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`

**Specific change from earlier PR revision**: The guard was expanded from fork-only to all parent-session use, and ownerless sessions are now protected. These address ClawSweeper review findings that the fork-only guard left cross-owner parent hierarchy, inherited auth-profile selection, and other parent-derived session state available through non-fork `parentSessionKey` use.

---

target.title: fix(memory): skip blank search provider bootstrap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory search handled blank or whitespace-only queries too late. The manager could initialize the provider, assert provider state, or bootstrap search work before the preflight returned an empty result.

## Why This Change Was Made

Blank query eligibility is a local preflight contract and should not require provider setup. This change shares query normalization with the existing preflight and short-circuits blank queries before provider/bootstrap work.

## User Impact

Whitespace-only memory searches return `[]` cheaply and deterministically, without requiring provider credentials, indexes, or search startup.

## Evidence

- Changed `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.ts`.
- Changed `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-preflight.ts`.
- Added `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.blank-query.test.ts` proving blank search returns `[]` before provider init, provider assertion, index check, or sync bootstrap.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-memory.config.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-preflight.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.blank-query.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
- `git diff --check upstream/main..HEAD`
- Controlled manager proof: `node --import tsx - <<'EOF' ...` invoked the actual `MemoryIndexManager.search` method with a whitespace-only query and provider/bootstrap counters.
- Normal manager proof: `node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'EOF' ...` constructed a real `MemoryIndexManager` through `MemoryIndexManager.get({ cfg, agentId: "main", purpose: "cli" })`, then ran a whitespace-only search.

## Proof

- Controlled proof query: whitespace-only.
- Controlled proof result: `resultCount: 0`, `results: []`.
- Provider/bootstrap counters all stayed zero: `ensureProviderInitialized: 0`, `assertRequiredProviderAvailable: 0`, `hasIndexedContent: 0`, `sync: 0`.
- Normal manager proof used a temporary workspace/state dir and `provider: "none"` with vector disabled to avoid external provider setup.
- Normal manager proof output:
  - `managerConstructed: true`
  - `purpose: "cli"`
  - `blankResultCount: 0`, `blankResults: []`
  - `beforeProviderState` and `afterProviderState`: `{ "mode": "pending", "requestedProvider": "none" }`
  - `beforeFiles: 0`, `afterFiles: 0`, `beforeChunks: 0`, `afterChunks: 0`
- This proves the blank-query preflight returns before provider initialization, provider availability assertion, index checks, or sync bootstrap on both the direct search method and a normally constructed manager path.


## Public CLI Proof

- Public CLI proof command: `pnpm openclaw memory search --query <whitespace> --json`, with `<whitespace>` equal to `" \n\t "` in a temporary `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, and workspace.
- Config used `agents.defaults.memorySearch.provider: "none"`, `store.vector.enabled: false`, and search/index watchers disabled, so a blank-query preflight must not need any embedding provider.
- Search exit: `0`.
- Search stdout:
  ```json
  {
    "results": []
  }
  ```
- Follow-up status command: `pnpm openclaw memory status --json` in the same fixture.
- Follow-up status core: `provider: "none"`, `requestedProvider: "none"`, `vector.enabled: false`, `files: 0`, `chunks: 0`, `dirty: true`.
- Workspace contents stayed `MEMORY.md` plus `memory/`; only the normal OpenClaw state SQLite files were created under the temporary state dir.
- This proves the public `openclaw memory search` path returns `[]` for a whitespace-only query before provider/bootstrap/index work.

## Required Provider CLI Comparison
Current-main baseline: `upstream/main@fab69517b3`. PR head: `a7cc3fc2096915f8956c529193bb32d4e6c30bbe`.

I ran the same public CLI command against current main and this PR head with an explicit required remote provider and intentionally absent credentials:

- Command: `pnpm openclaw memory search --query <whitespace> --json`
- Environment: `OPENAI_API_KEY` unset, isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`
- Config: `agents.defaults.memorySearch.provider: "openai"`, `model: "text-embedding-3-small"`, `fallback: "none"`, `sync.watch/onSessionStart/onSearch: false`, `store.vector.enabled: true`

Redacted output:

```text
upstream/main@fab69517b3
exitCode: 1
stderr: Memory search failed: No API key found for provider "openai" ... | missing-provider-auth
stdout: [ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.

PR head@a7cc3fc209
exitCode: 0
stdout: {
  "results": []
}
stderr: $ node scripts/run-node.mjs memory search --query '<whitespace>' --json
```

The same fixture's `pnpm openclaw memory status --json` output on both revisions reported `provider: "openai"`, `requestedProvider: "openai"`, `vector.enabled: true`, `files: 0`, `chunks: 0`, and `providerState.mode: "pending"`. That confirms this is not `provider: "none"` FTS-only proof: current main reaches required-provider auth before blank-query rejection, while the patched head returns the blank-query `[]` result before provider/bootstrap/index work.

target.title: fix(browser): refresh target after guarded existing-session actions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Existing-session `hover`, `scrollIntoView`, `drag`, `select`, and `fill` actions already run the post-interaction navigation guard, but their success responses kept the pre-action `targetId`. If one of those guarded actions triggered a renderer swap or same-URL target replacement, the next browser action could continue with a stale target.

## Why This Change Was Made
`click`, `clickCoords`, `type`, and `press` already resolve the current target after the same guarded existing-session path. This change applies that same response contract to the remaining guarded non-click interactions without changing unguarded or unsupported actions.

## User Impact
Browser agents using existing-session profiles get the current tab target after guarded hover, scroll, drag, select, and fill interactions. This reduces stale-target follow-up failures after navigation-like page changes.

## Evidence
- Added a regression test that simulates a guarded non-click interaction replacing the old target and verifies the response returns the replacement target.
- Focused tests:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.act.existing-session-navigation-guard.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.existing-session.test.ts`
- Touched-file checks:
  - `oxfmt --check extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.act.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.act.existing-session-navigation-guard.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.act.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.act.existing-session-navigation-guard.test.ts`

Current head: `e809e5a2f8183fd683b66eabff185fe055d0f43c`.

I ran a local live proof with real Chrome, real `chrome-devtools-mcp@latest`, and the real OpenClaw Browser HTTP routes. target.title: fix(codex): trigger model fallback on usage-limit promptError (#103734)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a Codex-backed turn hits the subscription usage limit, the Codex harness
returns a `promptError` in the attempt result instead of throwing. The host's
model fallback is throw-driven — it only engages when `FailoverError` is thrown.

The existing prompt-error handler already classifies the error and enters
`resolveRunFailoverDecision`.  However `shouldRotatePrompt` always returns true
for rate/billing limits, so the handler first tries **auth profile rotation** —
retrying the same harness with a different profile.  For harness-owned transports
(Codex) the limit is on the harness session, not the profile, so every rotation
fails identically.  This wastes the user's quota and burns retry budget
before fallback can engage.

Fixes #103734.

## Why This Change Was Made

One 8-line addition in `shouldRotatePrompt` (`failover-policy.ts`): when a
plugin harness owns the transport **and** the failover reason is `rate_limit`
or `billing`, skip profile rotation.  The decision falls through to
`fallback_model` in `resolveRunFailoverDecision`, which throws a `FailoverError`
that the outer fallback loop catches immediately.

Non-harness providers and non-limit errors are unchanged — they still rotate
profiles before falling back.

## User Impact

**Before:** Codex usage limit → profile rotation → all profiles fail →
run budget exhausted or model fallback with wasted quota.

**After:** Codex usage limit → `rate_limit` → skips rotation → falls back
to next configured model immediately.

## Evidence

### Live agent proof (Codex usage-limit → fallback model)

Primary `openai/gpt-5.5` (Codex) forced to return a redacted usage-limit error.
Fallback `zte/Qwen3-235B-A22B` configured.  Run completes on the fallback:

```
$ pnpm --filter openclaw openclaw agent --local \
    --message "say hello in one word" --session-key agent:proof:103734

# (1) Codex turn fails with usage-limit → decision=fallback_model
[agent/embedded] embedded run failover decision:
  stage=prompt decision=fallback_model reason=rate_limit
  from=openai/gpt-5.5

# (2) FailoverError thrown → model fallback loop catches it
[diagnostic] lane task error: FailoverError: You've reached your Codex
  subscription usage limit.

# (3) Fallback switches to zte/Qwen3-235B-A22B
[model-fallback/decision] decision=candidate_failed
  candidate=openai/gpt-5.5 reason=rate_limit
  next=zte/Qwen3-235B-A22B

# (4) Fallback model succeeds
[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response
  provider=zte model=Qwen3-235B-A22B status=200

[model-fallback/decision] decision=candidate_succeeded
  candidate=zte/Qwen3-235B-A22B

Hello

[agent] run ended with stopReason=stop
```

target.title: fix(shell): resolve pwsh.exe/.cmd/.bat on PATH for Windows shell discovery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, PowerShell 7 delivered via the Microsoft Store / App Execution Alias (and most portable installs) ships as `pwsh.exe`. `resolvePowerShellPath()` step 3 calls `resolveShellFromPath("pwsh")`, which only probed a **bare** `pwsh` with no extension. `fs.accessSync(entry/pwsh)` therefore returned `ENOENT`, so shell discovery fell through to Windows PowerShell 5.1 instead of using pwsh 7. This is the actual Windows pwsh resolution gap (distinct from the custom-shell `-c` args discussion in #104053).

## Evidence

Local reproduction on this Windows host (PowerShell 7.6.3 present only as the Store `pwsh.exe` alias, no `C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7`):
- `fs.accessSync("...\pwsh")` -> `ENOENT` (bare name missed by discovery)
- `fs.accessSync("...\pwsh.exe")` -> `OK` (extension probe hits it)
- After the fix, `resolveShellFromPath("pwsh")` returns the `pwsh.exe` path on PATH, and `resolvePowerShellPath()` prefers pwsh 7 over the 5.1 fallback.

This matches the source-level analysis: current main only looks for a bare `pwsh`, so a PATH entry containing only `pwsh.exe` is skipped before the Windows PowerShell 5.1 fallback (noted by the ClawSweeper review). The PR also adds Windows-only regression tests (guarded by `isWin` so Linux CI is unaffected): finds `pwsh.exe` when a bare `pwsh` is absent, prefers a bare `pwsh` match over `pwsh.exe` when both exist, and `resolvePowerShellPath()` resolves `pwsh.exe` on PATH instead of 5.1.

(Private paths and credentials redacted; this is a local OpenClaw gateway host.)

## Root cause

`resolveShellFromPath` joined the entry with the bare name and never tried executable extensions on Windows:

```ts
const candidate = path.join(entry, name); // only "pwsh", never "pwsh.exe"
```

## Fix

On `win32`, also probe `.exe`, mirroring the existing pattern already used by `resolveWindowsBashPath` (`"bash.exe"` / `"bash"`).

```ts
const executableExtensions = process.platform === "win32" ? [".exe"] : [];
const candidates = [base, ...executableExtensions.map((ext) => base + ext)];
```

**Scope note (addressed ClawSweeper review):** only `.exe` is added. `.cmd`/`.bat` are intentionally excluded because PTY execution (`createPtyAdapter`) spawns the resolved shell directly without child mode's `cmd.exe` wrapping, so a `pwsh.cmd` selected here could be chosen and then fail in PTY mode. `.exe` is directly executable in both child and PTY modes. Non-Windows behavior is unchanged.

This makes a Store/portable `pwsh.exe` discoverable on PATH, so `resolvePowerShellPath()` prefers pwsh 7 over 5.1.

## Test plan

Windows-only tests in `shell-utils.test.ts` (guarded by `isWin` so Linux CI is unaffected):
- finds `pwsh.exe` when a bare `pwsh` is absent
- prefers a bare `pwsh` match over `pwsh.exe` when both exist
- `resolvePowerShellPath()` resolves `pwsh.exe` on PATH instead of 5.1 when standard install dirs are empty

Existing tests unchanged; non-Windows `resolveShellFromPath` behavior preserved.

target.title: fix(agents): add size limit to LSP message parser
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: The LSP message parser accepted unbounded `Content-Length`
values. A malicious or misbehaving LSP server could send an arbitrarily
large `Content-Length` header, causing unbounded buffer allocation and
memory exhaustion. Additionally, a very long decimal `Content-Length`
(e.g., 400+ digits) causes `Number.parseInt` to return `Infinity`, which
was stored as an infinite drain counter — permanently suppressing all
future LSP output and leaving pending requests to time out.

**Root cause**: When `Content-Length` exceeded the 10 MB limit, the parser
only skipped the header + separator bytes but kept the declared body in
`session.buffer`. If the oversized body arrived across multiple stream
chunks, the buffer would grow unboundedly. For non-safe integer lengths
(`Infinity` from `parseInt`), the arithmetic computed `bodyStart + Infinity
= Infinity`, storing an infinite `oversizeDrainRemaining` that never
decrements. Additionally, when the final drain chunk exactly matched the
remaining byte count, the handler returned early without failing the
session, leaving the pending request to time out.

**Solution**: Add a 10 MB `Content-Length` limit that fully drains the
declared oversized body when the frame is completely buffered, or tracks
remaining bytes to skip via `session.oversizeDrainRemaining` when the body
arrives across chunks. Non-safe integer Content-Length values (Infinity)
are detected before drain arithmetic and signal a fatal protocol error.
Finite oversized frames (>10 MB but still a safe integer) trigger session
failure after dispatching any valid responses parsed before the oversized
frame — the associated pending request is rejected immediately instead of
waiting for the normal request timeout. The exact-match drain completion
boundary (`raw.length === oversizeDrainRemaining`) now falls through to
the session failure check instead of returning early.

**What changed**: `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts`
- `parseLspMessages`: accepts optional `oversizeDrainRemaining` out-param
  with `fatal` flag; on oversized frames drains the full frame or signals
  remaining bytes and sets the fatal flag. On non-safe integer
  Content-Length signals a fatal condition via NaN.
- `handleIncomingData`: drains `session.oversizeDrainRemaining` from raw
  stream data before appending to the parse buffer. Detects non-finite
  drain remaining or drained finite oversized frames and calls
  `failLspSession` after dispatching any completed responses parsed
  before the bad header. Fixed the exact-match drain boundary: changed
  `<=` to `<` so the exact-match case continues into session failure.
- `LspSession` type: added `oversizeDrainRemaining: number`,
  `oversizeDrainSeen: boolean`

**What did NOT change**: Valid message parsing, session lifecycle, tool
materialization — all unchanged for frames within the 10 MB limit.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: LSP message parser now closes three gaps:
1) fully drains finite oversized Content-Length frames (>10 MB) to
prevent memory exhaustion, 2) fails the session for non-safe integer
Content-Length (Infinity from parseInt) instead of permanently suppressing
all future LSP output, and 3) fails the session for finite oversized
frames after dispatching any valid responses parsed before the oversized
frame so the associated pending request is rejected immediately instead
of timing out.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 4.19.112, Node 22.19.0, pnpm 11.2.2

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
pnpm test src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All 18 tests pass, including 4 new
handler-level tests for finite oversized Content-Length session failure.

**Before-fix behavior (if applicable)**: Finite oversized frames (>10 MB)
were silently drained without failing the session, leaving the associated
pending request to time out after 10 seconds instead of failing
immediately. When the final drain chunk exactly matched the remaining
oversized body bytes, the handler returned early with a zero counter
without failing the session.

**After-fix evidence**:

All 18 tests pass:
```text
 ✓ bundle LSP runtime > oversized Content-Length handling (2)
 ✓ bundle LSP runtime > unsafe Content-Length handling (4)
 ✓ bundle LSP runtime > finite oversized Content-Length handling (4)
   ✓ sets fatal flag on parseLspMessages oversizeDrain
   ✓ fails LSP session on finite oversized frame through runtime handler path
   ✓ dispatches valid response before failing session on finite oversized frame
   ✓ fails the session when the final drain chunk exactly completes
```

**Real LSP server evidence**:

Tested against `vscode-json-languageserver` via stdio:

**Terminal output**:
```text
============================================================
L2 EVIDENCE: Real LSP server session via Content-Length framing
Server: vscode-json-languageserver
============================================================
Frame #1: {
  "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1,
  "result": {
    "capabilities": {
      "textDocumentSync": 2, "hoverProvider": true,
      "documentSymbolProvider": true, "foldingRangeProvider": true,
      "selectionRangeProvider": true
    }
  }
}
Frame #2: { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "result": null }
----------------------------------------
Initialize returned capabilities: ✅
Completion responded: ✅
CONCLUSION: Real LSP server session works end-to-end ✅
```

This proves the LSP message parser correctly handles real server I/O
with proper Content-Length framing.

**What was not tested**: A real LSP server sending non-safe Content-Length
or oversized (>10 MB) values — these are protocol violations that no
well-behaved LSP server would produce. The code paths are exercised
through handler-level tests that use the identical `handleIncomingData`
path the production LSP session uses.

**Risk level**: Low — non-safe and finite oversized Content-Length values
both trigger session failure after dispatching valid responses. All
existing message sizes within the 10 MB limit use the unchanged happy
path. merge-risk: low

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible — 10 MB is well above realistic LSP message sizes
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations — all 18 tests pass
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation — no docs changes needed
- [x] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary — none

target.title: fix(brave): resolve env secret refs for search key
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Brave web search accepted configured API keys, but env-backed SecretRefs in `tools.web.search.apiKey` were not resolved through the shared web-search credential path before falling back to `BRAVE_API_KEY`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Brave provider should treat direct API keys, env SecretRefs, and provider fallback env vars consistently with the shared web-search credential contract. This change routes Brave credential resolution through the existing shared resolver instead of duplicating a literal-only read.

## User Impact

target.title: fix(slack): suppress progress chrome sends
target.body:
## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of `chat.postMessage`
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies
- type automatic tool-progress payloads at the producer boundary with a closed generic plugin-SDK progress intent so Slack does not infer from arbitrary text

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: \`pnpm test\`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Evidence
Current head: `1e3f34f78d97ec5790a39b722f55b53e640488c5`.

- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false vitest run --project extension-codex extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` passed (149 tests)
- focused Slack replies + identity-fallback tests passed (85 tests)
- `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` passed (10 tests)
- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false tsgo:extensions` passed
- formatter check on touched files passed
- `git diff --check` passed

## Public SDK Contract
This PR uses a closed generic progress-intent contract on the reply-payload surface:

- shared field: `channelData.openclawProgressKind`
- generic tool progress kind: `TOOL_PROGRESS_KIND = "tool-progress"`
- generic predicate: `isToolProgressPayload`
- existing fast-mode kind remains: `FAST_MODE_AUTO_PROGRESS_KIND = "fast-mode-auto"`

Codex no longer exports Codex-named public progress symbols. Codex marks only transient automatic tool summaries with the generic `tool-progress` kind; completed/failed/verbose terminal output is left unmarked and remains deliverable. Callable public SDK budget was raised with the additive predicate.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
